node.title: Re: Is there a problem with using barewords as filehandles ?
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
What's so wrong with doing open RD, '<', 'file.txt' ?

I was involved with two discussions about this recently, [id://11115734] and [id://11117517], so here are my two cents. To summarize the disadvantages of bareword filehandles:

  • They don't protect against typos.
  • They're package-globals.
  • They clash with package names and subs.
  • If you do want to [doc://local]ize them, that comes with [id://11115735|even more] disadvantages.
  • Package-global filehandles usually go out of scope much later than lexicals, so the automatic [doc://close] doesn't really help.

I don't think that bareword filehandles should "never, ever" be used, and removing them would most likely break a lot of CPAN. But IMHO they shouldn't be used in new code, and newcomers should use lexicals instead. My understanding of Perl 7 is that it is an attempt to introduce defaults that are modern and reduce the cognitive load on the coder - sure, you can use bareword filehandles if you know what you're doing and are willing to manually check for all potentially typos and name clashes caused by them. In the beginning, I [id://11101494|used to] code without [doc://strict] and [doc://warnings], and I can still remember the amount of time I would spend proofreading my code for such issues.

use of barewords as filehandles will be disallowed in perl 7

My understanding of [https://youtu.be/6wPMh-3qYJM?t=2477|Sawyer's talk] is that the new default will be [mod://bareword::filehandles|no bareword::filehandles], and you are free to write use bareword::filehandles.
